examples.en: In the old days, news was sent far away by signal fires.
I saw a scene of lighting a signal fire on a mountaintop.
Beacon towers were built in high places.
When the signal fire went up, soldiers gathered.
I learned about the signal fire system at the museum.
This mountain is famous as a signal fire site.

explain: '횃불'은 손에 들거나 세워 두는 불이고, 봉화는 높은 산에서 연기와 불로 멀리 신호를 보내던 옛날 방식이에요. '봉화를 올리다', '봉화를 피우다'로 써요. 지금은 역사 이야기나 사극에서 주로 들어요.

phrases.en: The soldier raised a signal fire on the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '봉화'와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common partner phrase of 봉화.

phrases.en: An old beacon tower remains on the mountaintop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 봉화를 피우던 높은 곳이나 시설을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the high place or structure where beacon fires were lit.

phrases.en: I walked the night road holding a torch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 봉화와 달리 손에 들거나 세워 두는 불이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike 봉화, a fire you hold or stand up.

explain_en: '횃불' is a torch you hold or set up, while '봉화' was an old way of sending signals over long distances with smoke and fire from high mountains. It is used as '봉화를 올리다' or '봉화를 피우다'. Today you mostly hear it in history stories and historical dramas.

examples.en: The national anthem played before the sports match.
At school we memorized and sang the national anthem.

examples.ko: 올림픽에서 애국가가 울려 퍼지자 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: When the national anthem rang out at the Olympics, tears came.

examples.ko: 애국가는 모두 네 절로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: The national anthem has four verses in all.

examples.ko: 외국인 친구도 애국가를 한 절 불러 봤어요.
examples.en: My foreign friend also tried singing one verse of the anthem.

examples.ko: 행사 시작할 때 모두 일어나서 애국가를 들었어요.
examples.en: At the start of the event everyone stood up and listened to the anthem.

explain: '국가'는 나라 노래를 두루 부르는 말이고, 한국의 국가를 가리키는 이름이 '애국가'예요. 다른 나라의 국가를 말할 때는 '그 나라 국가'라고 해요. 보통 '애국가를 부르다/제창하다'라고 써요.

phrases.example: 행사에서 다 같이 일어나 애국가를 불러요.
phrases.en: At the event, everyone stands up and sings the national anthem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 애국가와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 동사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb phrase used with 애국가.

phrases.en: Do you know all the lyrics of the national anthem?
phrases.nuance_ko: 노래의 말, 곧 가사를 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the words of the anthem.

phrases.en: The national anthem rang out through the stadium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노래가 크게 들리는 장면을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the anthem sounding loudly in a place.

explain_en: 국가 is the general word for a national anthem, and 애국가 is the name of Korea's own. For another country's anthem, say 그 나라 국가. Common verbs are 부르다 and 제창하다.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 위인전기를 읽고 과학자가 되고 싶었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I read a biography of a great person and wanted to become a scientist.
I borrowed a biography of King Sejong from the library.
Even elementary school students can read this biography easily.

examples.ko: 위인전기에는 어려운 시기를 이겨 낸 이야기가 많아요.
examples.en: Biographies of great people have many stories of overcoming hard times.
I gave the child a biography as a gift.
I find novels more fun than biographies.

explain: 줄여서 '위인전'이라고도 해요. 주로 어린이 책이나 독서 이야기에서 나오고, 한 사람의 삶을 따라가며 교훈을 주는 책이라는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 동생은 위인전을 좋아해서 매주 한 권씩 읽어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling likes biographies and reads one every week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '위인전기'의 줄임말이고, 일상 대화에서는 이 말을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of '위인전기', and the more common one in everyday speech.

phrases.example: 위인전기 속 인물처럼 열심히 살고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to live hard like the people in biographies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책에 나오는 훌륭한 사람을 본받고 싶다는 이야기에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when wanting to follow the example of admirable people in books.

phrases.en: The author wrote a biography of Admiral Yi Sun-sin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 읽는 쪽이 아니라 책을 만드는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person writing, not reading.

explain_en: It is also shortened to '위인전'. It mostly comes up in talk about children's books and reading, and it suggests a book that follows one person's life and offers a lesson.

en: to be excavated; to be unearthed

examples.en: Old pottery was unearthed in this area.

examples.ko: 무덤에서 출토되는 유물은 역사 연구에 중요해요.
examples.en: Relics unearthed from tombs are important for historical research.
The excavated gold crown is on display at the museum.

examples.ko: 공사 중에 옛 동전이 출토돼서 공사가 멈췄어요.
examples.en: Old coins were found during construction, so the work stopped.

examples.ko: 이 칼은 어디에서 출토됐는지 알고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to know where this sword was unearthed.

examples.ko: 땅속에서 출토되면 먼저 보존 처리를 해요.
examples.en: Once something is unearthed, it first goes through preservation treatment.

explain: 땅속에 묻혀 있던 유물이나 화석이 나올 때 '유물이 출토되다'라고 말해요. 사람이 파는 일은 '발굴하다'이고, 나온 물건 쪽에서 보면 출토되다예요. '출토 유물', '출토지'처럼도 써요.

phrases.en: A gold crown was unearthed in Gyeongju.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유물이 출토되다'처럼 나온 물건을 주어로 해서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The excavated object is the subject, as in 'relics were unearthed'.

phrases.en: The museum exhibits excavated relics.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅에서 나온 유물을 하나의 명사로 묶어 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase for relics that came out of the ground.

phrases.en: No fossils have been unearthed here yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 발견되지 않았다는 부정 표현으로 쓸 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form used to say nothing has been found yet.

explain_en: Artifacts found in the ground, archaeology and museums, formal. You say '유물이 출토되다' when relics or fossils buried underground come out. Digging by people is '발굴하다', while 출토되다 views it from the side of the object that was found. It also appears in '출토 유물' and '출토지'.

t90.ax: Old pottery was unearthed in this area.

examples.ko: 햇빛에서 나오는 광선 중에는 눈에 보이지 않는 것도 있어요.
examples.en: Some of the rays from sunlight are invisible to the eye.

examples.ko: 강한 광선 때문에 눈이 부셔서 선글라스를 썼어요.
examples.en: The strong light was dazzling, so I put on sunglasses.

examples.ko: 영화 속 우주선이 푸른 광선을 쏘았어요.
examples.en: In the movie, the spaceship fired a blue beam.
A laser beam travels in a straight line.
We did an experiment where the direction of the light ray changes.
A thin ray of light comes in through the curtains.

explain: '빛'은 모든 밝음에 쓰고, 광선은 줄기처럼 곧게 뻗는 빛을 말할 때 써요. 과학 시간이나 영화에서 '레이저 광선', '태양 광선'처럼 나와요. 일상 대화에서 햇빛을 '광선'이라고 하면 딱딱하게 들려요.

phrases.example: 태양 광선이 너무 강해서 모자를 썼어요.
phrases.en: The sun's rays were so strong that I wore a hat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 햇빛을 과학적으로나 딱딱하게 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used for sunlight in a scientific or formal tone.

phrases.example: 영화 속 로봇이 눈에서 광선을 쏘았어요.
phrases.en: The robot in the movie shot a beam from its eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 만화에서 빛줄기를 내보낼 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in films and cartoons when something fires a beam of light.

phrases.en: Strong light rays are not good for the eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '강한'과 함께 써서 눈이나 피부에 영향을 주는 빛을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 강한 it describes intense light that affects eyes or skin.

explain_en: 빛 is used for any kind of light, while 광선 refers to light that travels straight like a thread. It appears in science class and movies as 레이저 광선 or 태양 광선. Calling sunshine 광선 in daily talk sounds stiff.

t90.ax: A laser beam travels in a straight line.

examples.en: Korea belongs to the temperate climate zone.
The plants that grow differ depending on the climate zone.

examples.ko: 열대 기후대에서는 일 년 내내 더워요.
examples.en: In a tropical climate zone it's hot all year round.
Try dividing the climate zones by color on the map.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 두 기후대가 만나는 곳이에요.
examples.en: This region is where two climate zones meet.
When the climate zone changes, people's way of life changes too.

explain: 지리 수업이나 설명문에서 많이 나와요. '열대, 온대, 냉대, 한대' 같은 말과 같이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '이 지역 날씨는 어때요?'처럼 말하는 편이에요.

phrases.example: 한국은 온대 기후대에 속해서 사계절이 뚜렷해요.
phrases.en: Korea belongs to the temperate climate zone, so it has four distinct seasons.
phrases.nuance_ko: '온대, 열대, 한대' 같은 말을 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Place words like '온대', '열대', '한대' before it.

phrases.example: 열대 기후대에서는 일 년 내내 더워요.
phrases.en: In the tropical climate zone, it is hot all year round.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더운 지역의 기후를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain the climate of hot regions.

phrases.example: 두 나라는 기후대가 달라서 먹는 음식도 달라요.
phrases.en: The two countries are in different climate zones, so their foods differ too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지역마다 날씨가 다르다는 것을 비교해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to compare how the weather differs between regions.
phrases.en_equiv: to be in different climate zones

explain_en: It appears a lot in geography classes and explanatory texts, together with words like 열대 (tropical), 온대 (temperate), 냉대 (cool-temperate) and 한대 (polar). In everyday talk people would just ask about the weather of a region instead.

examples.ko: 누에고치에서 가는 실을 뽑아 비단을 만들어요.
examples.en: Fine thread is drawn from silkworm cocoons to make silk.

examples.ko: 하얀 누에고치가 상자 안에 가득 있었어요.
examples.en: The box was full of white silkworm cocoons.
I touched a silkworm cocoon myself at the museum.
The pupa is changing inside the cocoon.

examples.ko: 누에고치 하나에서 아주 긴 실이 나와요.
examples.en: A very long thread comes out of a single cocoon.
The kids like the cocoon-shaped cushion.

explain: '고치'만 말해도 되지만 누에 이야기를 할 때는 '누에고치'라고 해요. 나방이나 나비의 애벌레가 만든 것도 '고치'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: The silkworm is making a white cocoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고치를 만드는 모습을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for the act of making a cocoon.

phrases.en: I watched them pull thread out of cocoons.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비단실을 만드는 과정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when describing how silk thread is made.
phrases.en_equiv: to reel thread from a cocoon

phrases.en: A pupa is growing inside the cocoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누에고치를 줄여서 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter way to say 누에고치.

explain_en: Specifically a silkworm cocoon, the source of silk thread. You can say just '고치', but when talking about silkworms, people say '누에고치'. The casing made by the larvae of moths or butterflies is also called '고치'.

t90.ax: The pupa is changing inside the cocoon.

en: to discharge; to release water; to release fish

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 댐이 물을 방류했어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so the dam released water.
The city releases salmon into the river every year.
The factory got caught secretly discharging wastewater.

examples.ko: 수문을 열어 물을 방류할 때는 미리 알려 줘요.
examples.en: When they open the floodgates and release water, they give notice in advance.

examples.ko: 아이들이 어린 물고기를 강에 방류하는 체험을 했어요.
examples.en: The kids had an experience releasing young fish into the river.

examples.ko: 댐이 방류하기 전에 주민들에게 문자를 보냈어요.
examples.en: They sent residents a text message before the dam released water.

explain: 물, 물고기, 폐수처럼 한꺼번에 흘려보내는 대상에 써요. 집에서 물고기를 놓아줄 때는 보통 '풀어 주다'라고 하고, '방류하다'는 댐이나 행사, 뉴스처럼 큰 규모의 일에 어울려요.

phrases.example: 공장이 몰래 폐수를 방류해서 문제가 됐어요.
phrases.en: The factory secretly discharged wastewater, which became a problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환경 문제 뉴스에서 자주 듣는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase in environmental news.

phrases.en: The dam's water was released this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '방류하다'의 피동 표현으로, 물이 나가는 쪽을 주어로 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form of 방류하다, with the water as the subject.

phrases.example: 시에서는 오늘 물을 방류하지 않기로 했어요.
phrases.en: The city decided not to release water today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방류를 하지 않겠다는 결정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a decision was made not to release water.

explain_en: Releasing water from dams, or young fish into rivers; news and official tone (댐 방류, 치어 방류) It is used for things sent out in bulk, such as water, fish or wastewater. When you let a pet fish go yourself, people usually say '풀어 주다', while '방류하다' fits large-scale matters such as dams, events and the news.

examples.ko: 문어 다리에는 빨판이 많이 달려 있어요.
examples.en: An octopus's legs have many suckers on them.
Thanks to its suckers, an octopus sticks to rocks.
You attach this toy to a window with its suction cup.

examples.ko: 물고기 중에는 빨판이 있는 종류도 있어요.
examples.en: Some kinds of fish have suckers.

examples.ko: 빨판을 이용해서 벽을 올라가는 동물이 있어요.
examples.en: There are animals that climb walls using suckers.

examples.ko: 빨판에 먼지가 묻으면 잘 안 붙어요.
examples.en: If dust gets on the suction cup, it doesn't stick well.

explain: 문어나 오징어 다리에 있는 동그란 부분을 말해요. 유리창에 붙이는 장난감이나 고리의 흡착 부분도 '빨판'이라고 부르는 경우가 많아요. 동물 이야기나 과학 수업에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: An octopus's suckers are really strong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물 이야기에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The pairing that appears most in animal talk.

phrases.en: Squid tentacles also have suckers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어디에 있는지 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain where the suckers are.

phrases.en: An octopus sticks to rocks with its suckers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빨판이 하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say what the suckers do.

explain_en: It refers to the round parts on the legs of an octopus or squid. People also often call the suction part of window-mounted toys or hooks a '빨판'. It comes up a lot in animal talk and science classes.

examples.en: The Grand Canyon is a very large canyon.
A clear river flows between the canyon walls.
We walked along the gorge.

examples.ko: 협곡 위에 긴 다리가 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: A long bridge stands over the canyon.

examples.ko: 깊은 협곡에서 바람 소리가 크게 들렸어요.
examples.en: The sound of the wind was loud in the deep gorge.
When it rains, the gorge becomes dangerous.

explain: '골짜기'는 산 사이의 낮은 곳을 두루 부르는 말이고, '협곡'은 좁고 깊고 벽이 가파른 곳이에요. 보통 큰 계곡이나 관광지를 말할 때 써요. 동네 뒷산의 작은 골짜기에는 잘 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: A river flows at the bottom of the deep canyon.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깊은'을 붙여 벽이 높고 가파른 모습을 그려 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 깊은 paints the picture of high, steep walls.

phrases.en: We crossed the canyon by a bridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다리나 줄로 협곡 건너편으로 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for getting to the other side of a canyon by a bridge or rope.

phrases.en: If you walk along the canyon, the scenery is great.
phrases.nuance_ko: 협곡 옆이나 안쪽 길을 걸어가는 여행 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in travel talk about walking a path beside or inside a canyon.

explain_en: 골짜기 is a general word for a low place between mountains, while 협곡 is narrow and deep with steep walls. It is usually used for large valleys or tourist sites. It is not used for a small valley on a local hill.

examples.en: That greeting is an expression people use out of custom.
Try to break away from conventional ways of thinking.
These days most holiday greetings are just customary.
If you only use stock expressions, your writing gets boring.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 줄거리가 너무 관습적이라서 새롭지 않아요.
examples.en: This movie's plot is so conventional that it doesn't feel fresh.
Try finding an unconventional method.

explain: 오랜 습관이나 관례에 따라 하는 것을 말해요. '전통적'은 중립적이거나 좋게 들리지만, '관습적'은 생각 없이 틀에 박힌 대로 한다는 느낌이 담길 때가 많아요. 반대 느낌은 '독창적', '파격적'이에요.

phrases.en: People customarily eat tteokguk on Lunar New Year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으로'를 붙여 오래된 습관대로 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 으로, it means doing something out of long-held habit.

phrases.en: '안녕하세요' is a conventional expression.
phrases.nuance_ko: 늘 정해진 대로 쓰는 말이나 인사를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe set phrases or greetings used in a fixed way.

phrases.example: 그 디자인은 관습적이지 않아서 눈에 띄어요.
phrases.en: That design is unconventional, so it stands out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 쓰면 틀에 박히지 않았다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the negative, it means not stuck in a mold.

explain_en: It describes doing something according to long-standing habit or convention. '전통적' sounds neutral or positive, while '관습적' often carries a feel of doing things by rote without thinking. The opposite feel is '독창적' or '파격적'.

examples.ko: 두 나라 군대가 국경에서 교전을 벌였어요.
examples.en: The armies of the two countries fought at the border.

examples.ko: 교전 때문에 많은 사람이 집을 떠났어요.
examples.en: Many people left their homes because of the fighting.
The news keeps reporting on the fighting.

examples.ko: 교전이 멈추고 나서야 마을에 평화가 왔어요.
examples.en: Peace only came to the village after the fighting stopped.

examples.ko: 어젯밤 교전으로 군인 몇 명이 다쳤어요.
examples.en: Several soldiers were hurt in last night's clash.
You cannot enter the combat zone.

explain: '전쟁'은 나라 사이의 크고 긴 싸움이고, '교전'은 무기를 들고 실제로 맞붙어 싸우는 순간에 초점이 있어요. 뉴스에서 '교전이 벌어지다', '교전이 멈추다'처럼 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: Fighting broke out near the border all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 싸움이 시작되었다고 전할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation in news reports for fighting breaking out.

phrases.en: The soldiers are in combat right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-중'을 붙여 지금 싸우는 중이라는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-중' means fighting is going on right now.

phrases.en: The fighting stopped after just one day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 싸움이 끝났거나 잠시 멈췄다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the fighting has ended or paused.

explain_en: Armed fighting between forces — news and military, formal, neutral. 전쟁 is a big, long war between nations, while 교전 focuses on the moment armed forces actually clash. You often hear it in the news as 교전이 벌어지다 or 교전이 멈추다.

t90.ax: You cannot enter the combat zone.

examples.en: That is far too outdated an idea.
That advertisement is a bit outdated.

examples.ko: 아버지의 구시대적 생각이 답답할 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes my father's old-fashioned thinking is frustrating.
It's an outdated rule, so everyone says we should change it.

examples.ko: 이런 구시대적 제도가 아직도 있다니 놀라워요.
examples.en: I'm surprised that an outdated system like this still exists.

examples.ko: 구시대적 방법으로는 요즘 손님을 잡기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to attract today's customers with outdated methods.

explain: 생각, 제도, 관행, 방식이 시대에 뒤떨어졌다고 비판할 때 써요. 물건이나 스타일이 예스러울 때 쓰는 '구식'보다 평가가 더 강해요. 보통 '구시대적 발상', '구시대적 관행'처럼 명사 앞에 붙여요.

phrases.en: Outdated practices should disappear now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '관행'은 오래 이어진 일하는 방식이에요. 회사 이야기에 잘 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: 관행 means a long-standing way of doing things, common in workplace talk.

phrases.en: That way of thinking is too outdated.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-이다'를 붙여 서술어로도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can add -이다 to use it as a predicate.

phrases.en: Try to get away from outdated thinking.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-인'을 붙이면 명사 앞에서 자연스럽게 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -인 lets it modify a noun naturally.

explain_en: Use it to criticize ideas, systems, practices, or methods as behind the times. It is a stronger judgment than '구식', which is used for old-fashioned things or styles. It is usually placed before a noun, as in '구시대적 발상' or '구시대적 관행'.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 근대적인 계획에 따라 만들어졌어요.
examples.en: This city was built following a modern plan.
The modern education system began at that time.

examples.ko: 그 공장은 근대적 설비를 갖추고 있어요.
examples.en: That factory is equipped with modern facilities.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 근대적 가치관을 잘 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This novel shows modern values well.
The design of this building is very modern in style.
I was surprised that my grandmother's thinking was so modern.

explain: '근대적 + 명사'로 쓰고, '근대적이다'처럼 서술어로도 써요. '근대'는 옛날과 오늘날 사이의 시기라서, '근대적'은 '현대적'(지금 느낌)과 다르게 그 시기의 제도나 생각을 가리킬 때 써요.

phrases.en: A modern system was first created at that time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '근대적인'을 명사 앞에 붙여 그 시기의 새로운 방식을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun, 근대적인 refers to a new way of that period.

phrases.example: 이 건물은 그 시대에 아주 근대적이었어요.
phrases.en: This building was very modern for its time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서술어로 쓰면 그 시기에는 새롭고 앞선 모습이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a predicate, it means something was new and advanced for that period.

phrases.en: He was a person with a modern way of thinking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각이나 태도가 옛날 방식에서 벗어난 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when thinking or attitude has moved away from old ways.

explain_en: Modern in the historical sense, tied to the modernization era (근대적 사고방식) It is used before a noun as '근대적 + noun' and also as a predicate like '근대적이다'. '근대' is the period between old times and today, so '근대적' points to systems or ideas of that period, unlike '현대적', which means modern in today's sense.

t90.ax: This novel shows modern values well.
